ety.text: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *pstḗn Proto-Indo-European *pstén-o-s Proto-Indo-Iranian *(p)stánas Sanskrit स्तन॑ (stána) Prakrit थण (thaṇa) Hindi थन Inherited from Prakrit थण (thaṇa), from Sanskrit स्तन॑ (stána). Doublet of स्तन (stan) and पिस्तान (pistān).
Literally "to have one's nose cut off", probably in reference to the fate of Shurpanakha in the Hindu mythological tale Ramayana who had her nose cut off by Lakshman, brother of Rama.
